quick_skim.title: TurboWAM: Learning What Matters for Fast World Action Models
quick_skim.abstract: World action models have demonstrated promising performance in robot policy learning, yet their high inference latency remains a critical bottleneck for real-world deployment. Recent approaches have sought to improve inference efficiency by reducing test-time future-frame imagination or accelerating action prediction. However, these methods often leverage representations from all video world model layers without explicitly considering their varying relevance to action prediction, leading to redundant computation and suboptimal representation utilization. In this work, we propose TurboWAM, a fast world action model that efficiently aggregates structured world representations conditioned on action predictions. Specifically, TurboWAM introduces a structured world representation aggregation module that adaptively fuses representations from different world model layers according to their relevance to the evolving action denoising state. Furthermore, TurboWAM employs a structured action supervision mechanism that adaptively modulates gradients from action supervision across different world model layers during backward propagation, facilitating world representation learning. During inference, by reducing the number of world model layers executed and caching relevant representations across action denoising steps, TurboWAM substantially reduces computational overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that TurboWAM achieves low inference latency while maintaining competitive task success rates compared with state-of-the-art methods.

quick_skim.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: static problems
quick_skim.abstract: We consider the coordination of autonomous vehicles at unsignalized intersections, where trajectory planning and crossing-order decisions are intrinsically coupled, thereby making their simultaneous optimization intractable in practice. To this end, we propose a heuristic based on a hierarchical structure consisting of a series of nonlinear programs (NLP) in the lower level, which optimizes trajectories of each vehicle for a given crossing order, and a high-level heuristic to design new crossing schedules that exploits sensitivity information from the lower-level NLPs. Extensive numerical simulations across a broad range of traffic scenarios demonstrate that our strategy achieves substantially improved scheduling with respect to first-in-first-out ordering while preserving computational tractability.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: coordination of multiple autonomous vehicles at intersections
quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: At unsignalized intersections trajectory planning couples with crossing order. This paper proposes a hierarchical heuristic with lower-level NLPs and an upper-level schedule search exploiting sensitivity, improving over first-in-first-out.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 无信号交叉口下，自动驾驶车辆的轨迹规划与通行顺序决策强耦合，同时优化难以求解。作者提出分层启发式框架，下层用非线性规划为给定通行顺序优化各车轨迹，上层借助灵敏度信息设计新的通行顺序。大量交通场景仿真表明该策略的调度效果显著优于先到先服务基线。该工作为多车协同通行提供了可扩展的协调优化方法，与多机器人协调系统高度相关。

quick_skim.title: A heuristic for optimal coordination of autonomous vehicles: real-time algorithms
quick_skim.abstract: When coordinating connected and automated vehicles at an unsignalized intersection, the crossing order and the vehicle trajectories must be decided jointly. For a fixed crossing order, the problem can be formulated conveniently in a bi-level form where each vehicle solves its own optimal control problem, whose optimal value is a function of its entry and exit times, and a coordinator optimizes these times subject to precedence constraints. We compute the first and second order sensitivities of lower-level problems, which are required to solve the upper-level problem, by means of algorithmic differentiation using the real-time software package \texttt{acados}. This implementation exploits tailored algorithms to obtain a computationally efficient implementation of the optimal coordination algorithm. We validate our implementation in numerical simulations that demonstrate both real-time feasibility and effectiveness of our algorithm.

quick_skim.title: Open-World Object Motion Anticipation via Meta-Learned Semantic Adaptation
quick_skim.abstract: Anticipating the motion of nearby objects is critical for safe and efficient robot navigation. Without a proper understanding of what may move, a robot may plan overly conservative, inefficient trajectories to guarantee safety, or it may be overly risky, resulting in unacceptable collisions. While tracking and predicting the motion of known objects has seen significant progress, little research addresses how a robot should adapt online to novel objects, including anticipating how one object may move another (e.g., a person operating a forklift to move a pallet). To enable this capability, we propose a meta-learned graph neural network that leverages a semantic, geometric, and relational history of objects to accurately predict, from a few online observations, when objects will begin to move in new environments. We demonstrate that our method, which is trained only in simulation, accurately anticipates the motion of objects unseen at training time, transfers to hardware without any fine-tuning, and outperforms a vision-language model and a class-frequency baseline in both simulation and hardware experiments. Our method's accurate prediction enables collision-free traversals in a closed-loop navigation simulation, while remaining within four seconds of the fastest, collision-prone planner.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: A meta-learned graph neural network anticipates motion of novel objects and object-object interactions from few online observations, enabling safer robot navigation in open-world settings.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 机器人导航需要预判周围物体运动，但面对新物体（如人驾驶叉车搬运托盘）时难以在线适应，易导致过保守或过冒险的轨迹。本文提出元学习图神经网络，利用物体的语义、几何与关系历史，从少量在线观测中预测新物体及物体间交互引发的运动。实验表明该方法提升了开放世界中的运动预判能力。这为动态仓储等环境下的安全高效导航提供了支持。
